A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LIDDIA and the same 30-target benchmark. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison; relocated material and redrawn molecular structures can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecule-generation evaluations across 30 targets, numerical benchmark results in Table 2, action-trajectory analyses and an EGFR case study.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds ablations, baseline results, toxicity predictions and molecular case analyses in Section 5.2 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The four-component framework, Pocket2Mol generation, GraphGA optimization, screening and termination procedure remain unchanged. DeepSeek-R1 and the deterministic loop are introduced as evaluation variants, without revising the core proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: The same 30 targets, PDB structures and disease coverage are retained. AR/NR3C4 was already included in v1. The additional case studies and toxicity assessments concern existing coverage; TargetDiff's 29-target subset is an evaluation-setting difference.

E2.justification: Table A3 adds TargetDiff, DecompDiff and a deterministic control without reasoning while retaining all six original baselines. This substantially expands comparisons of molecular generation and reasoning. The new AR case adds ligand/drug comparisons, whereas Gefitinib disappears from the focused EGFR comparison.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs replace LLM components with DeepSeek-R1 and test a deterministic GENERATE-then-OPTIMIZE/SCREEN loop with k=10. Additional assessments introduce ADMET-AI toxicity endpoints and chemical filters. TargetDiff excludes EZH2 and uses 29 pockets. The original framework's ten-action limit and HQ/TSR criteria remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds reasoning-removal and backend ablations, toxicity assessment, explicit failure analysis, an AR docking/filter case study and chemical scrutiny of the EGFR examples. These substantially extend investigation of effectiveness and failure conditions. The original action-trajectory analysis is retained in Appendix D.3 rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests for its experimental results. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: All original Table 2 numerical columns are retained in Table A3. New TSR results include DeepSeek-R1 at 73.3%, the deterministic control at 30.0%, TargetDiff at 13.8% over 29 targets and DecompDiff at 13.3%. New toxicity and molecular findings include NL-1's Vina score of -8.81 kcal/mol. The twelve-molecule EGFR comparison grid is removed, while its two illustrated examples remain.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same novelty and diversity formulas and HQ/TSR definitions. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and the new analyses do not introduce substantive mathematical developments.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion replace the highlighted promising EGFR candidates with one AR/NR3C4 candidate. The central autonomous-agent contribution, success on over 70% of 30 targets and exploration/exploitation claims remain.

C2.justification: v1 promotes its illustrated EGFR molecules as promising candidates; v2 identifies enol instability, fulvene reactivity and phototoxicity concerns in those examples and explains why computational filters cannot replace medicinal chemists. It also adds docking interpretations, a pocket-constraint hypothesis for failures and substantive qualifications about practical deployment and validation.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-dataset availability statement with a repository link and identifies tools used for toxicity and chemical-filter assessments. It also discloses TargetDiff's EZH2 implementation failure. The original prompts, generation settings and core implementation description are retained.

R1.justification: The supporting literature expands substantially into chemical-filter rules, molecular instability and phototoxicity, AR/STING biology, and the newly evaluated generation methods and DeepSeek-R1. This broadens the paper's scientific grounding beyond its earlier emphasis. Section 2's agent positioning remains largely unchanged; DiffSMol's publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: The results narrative is substantially reorganized: a dedicated ablation section is introduced, detailed trajectories and case studies move into Appendix D, and limitations move from Section 7 to Appendix A. Case-study and limitations passages are extensively rewritten, and the abstract and conclusion are refocused, although most framework prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 switches to a single-column layout, redraws Figure 1, redistributes the main results into Figure 2, Table 2 and expanded landscape Table A3, and merges the action-summary figures. It adds toxicity and docking displays and removes the EGFR comparison grid. New Figure 2c incorrectly labels SAS and VNA thresholds with greater-than inequalities despite the retained less-than definitions.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses by adding reasoning/backend controls and newer baselines, and by exposing chemical liabilities in the EGFR molecules that v1 presented as promising. Appendix D.6 substantially improves the interpretation of computational success and its practical limits. The AR analysis and code/data access statement provide further support. Mixed toxicity predictions still warrant more caution than the new safety language conveys, and Figure 2c introduces labeling errors, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial gains in evidence and scientific qualification.
